A mapping rule

Source: R/mapping_rules.R
mapping_rule.Rd

The tuples of the mapping are the natural join of the tables named in of, in order (tables without a shared column form a cross product), kept where they match every table in gate (semi-joins) and none in minus (anti-joins), projected to cols and made unique. A name resolves to an embedded table in tables, else to a mapping of the model, else to a set of the model (a one-column table under the set's name). Columns of a join that are not in cols are hidden: they take part in the joins and are dropped by the projection.

Usage

mapping_rule(of, gate = NULL, minus = NULL, tables = NULL, cols = NULL)

materialise_rule(model, rule)

Arguments

of

Character; the tables joined.

gate, minus

Character; tables whose matching tuples are kept, or dropped. Matching is on the columns shared with the join.

tables

A named list of data frames embedded in the rule; small tables that are not symbols of the model.

cols

Character; the columns of the result, in the mapping's dimension order. new_mapping() fills it from dims when NULL.

model

The model whose mappings and sets the rule names; may be an empty list when every leaf is embedded.

rule

An mm_rule.

Value

An object of class mm_rule; its hash identifies the rule's content (names and embedded tables).

A data.frame of character columns rule$cols, one row per tuple.

Examples

pf <- data.frame(tech = c("coal", "wind"), frame = c("ANNUAL", "HOUR"))
fs <- data.frame(frame = c("ANNUAL", "HOUR", "HOUR"),
                 slice = c("y", "h1", "h2"))
r <- mapping_rule(of = c("pf", "fs"), tables = list(pf = pf, fs = fs),
                  cols = c("tech", "slice"))
m <- new_mapping("mTechSlice", dims = c("tech", "slice"), rule = r)
materialise_rule(list(), r)
#>   tech slice
#> 1 coal     y
#> 2 wind    h1
#> 3 wind    h2
